learning_outcomes.text: Students know and understand essential principles of software development for technical systems. They know lifecycle models and can implement them correctly. They are able to systematically and documented analyze software requirements and implement them object-oriented.

Different approaches to software development for technical systems are understood. Traditional and modern procedural models and their milestone results and documentation forms are mastered. Important basic functions can be implemented independently. The handling of typical error situations is correctly implemented. The use of external class libraries and the software-technical connection to networks are mastered. In development groups, modules are developed and tested separately and then integrated. The essential requirements for system tests and their documentation are mastered.

Students understand software development as part of a Systems Engineering approach. They recognize the connection between the respective development task and its embedding in a project team that works collaboratively to achieve project goals. They see the value of early documented agreements and specifications.

Students who have successfully completed this module have knowledge of the essential aspects of developing software for technical systems and can apply this in the creation of software concepts and implementations.

Students who have successfully completed this module can analyze and document requirements for innovative products and new technological possibilities. They understand how to consider all aspects of modern technical systems, including their distribution, interfaces, and resource-efficient realization during development.

Students who have successfully completed this module can cooperate with groups from other disciplines and explain their own technical aspects clearly. They can structure, document, and present their work results at various stages of group collaboration.

Students can adequately assess their individual qualification profile regarding the analysis and development of technical systems and can differentiate and soundly justify their technological and methodological decisions.

syllabus_topics: Structure of requirements, system, and test specifications
Object-oriented analysis and design with UML (Unified Modeling Language)
Aspects of resource-efficient development of software-based technical products
assessment_rules: The final grade is determined by a portfolio examination: four written assignments, each worth 15 points, and a term paper worth 40 points, totaling 100 points. The project report involves a written report of approximately 10-15 pages and a related explanation of approximately 10 minutes. The unmarked experimental work consists of approximately 4-6 experiments in total.
